facts.statement: Divisor latches are accessed by setting LCR bit 7 to 1
facts.quote: The divisor latches can be accessed by setting the 7th bit of LCR to ‘1’.

facts.statement: Two divisor bytes form one 16-bit register accessed as single number
facts.quote:
The 2 bytes form one 16-bit register, which is
internally accessed as a single number.

facts.statement: Divisor register resets to 0 which disables all serial I/O operations
facts.quote:
The register is set to the default value of 0 on reset, which
disables all serial I/O operations in order to ensure explicit setup of the register in the
software.

facts.statement: Programmed divisor equals system clock speed divided by 16 times desired baud rate
facts.quote: The value set should be equal to (system clock speed) / (16 x desired baud rate).

facts.statement: Divisor programming writes MSB first and LSB last with counter starting on LSB write
facts.quote:
The internal counter starts to work when the LSB of DL is written, so when setting the
divisor, write the MSB first and the LSB last.

facts.statement: Divisor LSB byte is at WISHBONE pin address 0 with 8-bit width
facts.quote: Divisor Latch Byte 1 (LSB) 0 8 RW The LSB of the divisor

facts.statement: Divisor MSB byte is at WISHBONE pin address 1 with 8-bit width
facts.quote: Divisor Latch Byte 2 1 8 RW The MSB of the divisor

facts.statement: Divisor registers are accessed when LCR DLAB bit 7 is set to 1
facts.quote:
The registers can be accessed when the 7th (DLAB) bit of the Line Control Register is set
to ‘1’.
